name: working-memory
description: Workstream-aware session journal for Michael's hub workspace.

commands.title: Download and install the latest release of Working Memory

languageModelTools.name: wm_list_workstreams
languageModelTools.modelDescription: List workstreams from the Working Memory journal database. Returns each workstream's id, slug, title, status (open|closed), opened_at and closed_at (unix seconds), closure note, deleted_at, and session_count (excluding soft-deleted sessions). Use to discover which workstreams exist before starting a session or appending entries. Soft-deleted workstreams are hidden unless include_deleted is true.
languageModelTools.userDescription: List workstreams from the Working Memory journal

include_deleted.description: Include soft-deleted workstreams. Defaults to false.

languageModelTools.name: wm_get_workstream
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Fetch a single workstream by slug or id, along with its sessions (session_id, started_at, ended_at, summary, entry_count, deleted_at), total_entries count, and `focused_topics` (subset of linked topics where the workstream→topic link is currently focused; each entry is { slug, title, status, linked_at }). Mirrors what the Working Memory virtual document shows but as structured JSON. Provide exactly one of `slug` or `id`. Soft-deleted children are hidden unless include_deleted is true.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Get a workstream and its sessions

id.description: The workstream numeric id (alternative to slug).

include_deleted.description: Include soft-deleted child sessions/entries. Defaults to false.

languageModelTools.name: wm_create_workstream
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Create a new workstream. Slug must be unique across all workstreams (including soft-deleted ones). Title is the human-readable name. Status is a lifecycle value: 'queue', 'progress' (default), or 'backlog' place it in the matching Active-tab section; 'closed' archives it and stamps closed_at. Optional: pass topic_slug to pin a topic to this workstream at birth (same effect as calling wm_link_workstream_topic after). Pair with focused: true to create a workstream that is already focused on a topic — this is the canonical one-call way to set up a topic-focused workstream. All operations are in a single transaction: if the topic link fails (e.g. topic not found), the workstream is not created. Returns the created workstream row plus an optional topic_link summary.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Create a new workstream

title.description: Human-readable title, e.g. 'MCP Integration Work'. Keep it short and scannable (aim for ~6 words / ~48 chars). Lead with the task's common vernacular — the noun/verb you'd actually say out loud (e.g. 'Drag & drop topics', not 'Implement drag-and-drop reordering for topics in the panel'). Drop framing words ('Implement', 'Add support for', 'Feature to…'), trailing punctuation, and restated context. Prefer '<verb> <object>' or a bare noun phrase.

status.description: Initial lifecycle status. One of 'queue' | 'progress' | 'backlog' (Active-tab sections) or 'closed' (archived). Defaults to 'progress'.

topic_slug.description: Optional kebab-case slug of an existing topic to pin to this workstream at creation. Pair with focused: true to create a workstream that is immediately focused on that topic.

focused.description: Only meaningful when topic_slug is provided. true → set focused = 1 on the workstream-topic link (marks the topic as the workstream's current focus).

languageModelTools.name: wm_update_workstream
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Partially update a workstream identified by slug. Any of title, status, closure can be changed. Status is a lifecycle value: 'queue' | 'progress' | 'backlog' move it between Active-tab sections; 'closed' archives it (stamps closed_at if currently null). Moving from 'closed' back to an active section clears closed_at. Returns the updated row.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Update a workstream's title, status, or closure note

slug.description: Slug of the workstream to update.

title.description: New title. Keep it short and scannable (aim for ~6 words / ~48 chars). Lead with the task's common vernacular — the noun/verb you'd actually say out loud (e.g. 'Drag & drop topics', not 'Implement drag-and-drop reordering for topics in the panel'). Drop framing words ('Implement', 'Add support for', 'Feature to…'), trailing punctuation, and restated context. Prefer '<verb> <object>' or a bare noun phrase.

status.description: New lifecycle status. 'queue' | 'progress' | 'backlog' move it between Active-tab sections; 'closed' archives it and stamps closed_at if unset.

closure.description: Closure note (typically set when status flips to closed).

languageModelTools.name: wm_delete_workstream
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Soft-delete a workstream and cascade soft-delete to all its sessions and entries. Sets deleted_at = now on every affected row in a single transaction; the rows remain in the DB but are hidden from list/get/search calls unless include_deleted is true. Affected entries are also removed from the FTS index. Returns counts of affected rows per table.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Soft-delete a workstream (cascades to its sessions and entries)

slug.description: Slug of the workstream to soft-delete.

languageModelTools.name: wm_restore_workstream
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Restore a soft-deleted workstream by clearing its deleted_at. Restores only the workstream row itself — sessions and entries remain soft-deleted and must be restored individually. Returns count of restored rows. No-op (returns zeros) if the workstream is not currently soft-deleted.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Restore a soft-deleted workstream

slug.description: Slug of the workstream to restore.

languageModelTools.name: wm_start_session
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Start a new journaling session within a workstream. Generates a UUID v4 session_id if not provided. Sets started_at = now. Returns the session row; remember the session_id to append entries with wm_append_entry and to close it with wm_end_session.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Start a new journaling session

summary.description: Optional opening summary; usually written at session end via wm_end_session.

session_id.description: Optional explicit session_id. If omitted, a UUID v4 is generated.

chat_ref.description: Optional reference to the chat that produced this session — typically the value of the VSCODE_TARGET_SESSION_LOG env var (a path to the per-chat debug-logs folder) or any other stable per-chat identifier. Rendered on the session virtual doc; never fabricated.

languageModelTools.name: wm_end_session
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Close a session by stamping ended_at = now. Optionally updates the summary (1-2 lines that describe what the session accomplished). Returns the updated session.
languageModelTools.userDescription: End a journaling session

languageModelTools.name: wm_get_session
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Fetch a session plus all its entries in chronological order. Soft-deleted entries are hidden unless include_deleted is true.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Get a session and its entries

include_deleted.description: Include soft-deleted entries. Defaults to false.

languageModelTools.name: wm_delete_session
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Soft-delete a session and cascade soft-delete to all its entries in one transaction. Affected entries are removed from the FTS index. Returns counts of affected rows.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Soft-delete a session (cascades to its entries)

languageModelTools.name: wm_restore_session
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Restore a soft-deleted session by clearing its deleted_at. Restores only the session row itself — entries remain soft-deleted and must be restored individually with wm_restore_entry. Returns count of restored rows. No-op (returns zeros) if the session is not currently soft-deleted.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Restore a soft-deleted session

languageModelTools.name: wm_append_entry
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Append a single journal entry to a session. This is the workhorse tool — call it after every meaningful event (chat, command, decision, file change, system action, frustration, fact, idea, question). Body is the entry text — prefer a single line prefixed with the entry type, e.g. 'decision: chose option 2 because…'. Timestamp defaults to now (unix seconds). Returns the new entry's id and timestamp.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Append an entry to a session journal

session_id.description: The session_id this entry belongs to.

body.description: Entry text. One or two lines. Prefer prefixing with the entry type.

created_by.description: Actor that produced this entry. Use your agent name (e.g. 'orchestrator', 'executor'), 'system' for Working Memory itself, or 'human' for a direct user write. Must not be empty or end with '*'.

timestamp.description: Optional override (unix seconds). Defaults to now.

languageModelTools.name: wm_search_entries
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Full-text search across entries using SQLite FTS5. The `query` accepts FTS5 MATCH syntax (e.g. 'sqlite OR fts5', '"exact phrase"', 'work*'). Returns matches with a highlighted snippet (delimited by << and >>), workstream slug + title, session_id, and timestamp. Soft-deleted entries/sessions/workstreams are always excluded. Optionally scope to a single workstream by slug. Default limit 25, max 200.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Search journal entries (FTS5)

languageModelTools.name: wm_delete_entry
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Soft-delete a single entry by id. Removes it from the FTS index and sets deleted_at = now in one transaction. Returns the count of affected rows.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Soft-delete a journal entry

entry_id.description: Numeric id of the entry to soft-delete.

languageModelTools.name: wm_restore_entry
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Restore a single soft-deleted entry by id. Clears deleted_at and re-inserts the entry into the FTS index in one transaction. Returns the count of restored rows. Throws if the entry does not exist or is not currently soft-deleted.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Restore a soft-deleted journal entry

entry_id.description: Numeric id of the entry to restore.

languageModelTools.name: wm_list_topics
languageModelTools.modelDescription: List topics (durable, evolving subjects) with link counts. Each topic returns slug, title, status (open|closed), topic_type (discriminator; defaults to 'topic' for legacy rows), body, created_at/updated_at/deleted_at, workstream_count (active workstream links), and entry_count (active entry links). Filter by status, optionally scope to one workstream via workstream_slug (returns only topics linked to that workstream), and optionally filter to a single topic_type. Soft-deleted topics are hidden unless include_deleted is true. Valid topic_type values live in the `topic_types` table — call wm_list_topic_types to enumerate them.
languageModelTools.userDescription: List topics from the journal

include_deleted.description: Include soft-deleted topics. Defaults to false.

workstream_slug.description: Optional: only return topics linked to this workstream.

topic_type.description: Optional: filter to a single topic_type id. Any id from the `topic_types` table — call wm_list_topic_types to see valid values.

languageModelTools.name: wm_get_topic
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Fetch a topic by slug, plus its linked workstreams (active links), up to 25 most recent linked entries (newest first), its DAG neighborhood: `parents` (active parent topics) and `children` (active child topics), each as { slug, title, status }, and `focused_in_workstreams` (subset of linked workstreams where this topic is currently focused; each entry is { slug, title }). Mirrors what the topic virtual document shows but as structured JSON. Use to inspect a topic before editing it, linking new entries, or rewiring its parent/child relationships.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Get a topic with its linked workstreams and recent entries

include_deleted.description: Include soft-deleted topic. Defaults to false.

languageModelTools.name: wm_create_topic
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Create a topic. slug is required and must be unique across all topics (including soft-deleted ones). title is optional and defaults to a humanized version of the slug. body is freeform markdown. status defaults to 'open'. topic_type defaults to 'topic' — call wm_list_topic_types to enumerate valid ids. Optional auto-link parameters (all run in the same transaction as the insert; any failure rolls back the entire call): workstream_slug — pin the topic to a workstream (same as calling wm_link_workstream_topic after); focused — only meaningful with workstream_slug; marks the topic as focused in that workstream; entry_id — tag an entry with the new topic (same as wm_link_entry_topic, which also auto-creates the workstream link for the entry's workstream); parent_slug — link to one or more parent topics (string or array of strings; same as wm_link_topic_parent for each).
languageModelTools.userDescription: Create a new topic

title.description: Optional human-readable title. Defaults to humanized slug. Keep it short and scannable (aim for ~6 words / ~48 chars). Lead with the task's common vernacular — the noun/verb you'd actually say out loud (e.g. 'Drag & drop topics', not 'Implement drag-and-drop reordering for topics in the panel'). Drop framing words ('Implement', 'Add support for', 'Feature to…'), trailing punctuation, and restated context. Prefer '<verb> <object>' or a bare noun phrase.

topic_type.description: Any id from the `topic_types` table — call wm_list_topic_types to see valid values. Defaults to 'topic'.

workstream_slug.description: Optional: pin the new topic to an existing workstream at creation. Same effect as calling wm_link_workstream_topic after, but atomic.

focused.description: Only meaningful when workstream_slug is provided. true → set focused = 1 on the workstream-topic link.

entry_id.description: Optional: tag an existing journal entry with the new topic at creation. Also auto-creates the workstream link for that entry's workstream.

parent_slug.description: Optional: link the new topic to one or more parent topics at creation. Accepts a single slug string or an array of slug strings. Each link has the same effect as a wm_link_topic_parent call.

languageModelTools.name: wm_update_topic
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Partially update a topic by slug. Any of title, body, status, topic_type can be changed. Bumps `updated_at`. Returns the updated topic row. Valid topic_type values live in the `topic_types` table — call wm_list_topic_types to enumerate them.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Update a topic's title, body, status, or type

slug.description: Slug of the topic to update.

title.description: New title. Keep it short and scannable (aim for ~6 words / ~48 chars). Lead with the task's common vernacular — the noun/verb you'd actually say out loud (e.g. 'Drag & drop topics', not 'Implement drag-and-drop reordering for topics in the panel'). Drop framing words ('Implement', 'Add support for', 'Feature to…'), trailing punctuation, and restated context. Prefer '<verb> <object>' or a bare noun phrase.

topic_type.description: Any id from the `topic_types` table — call wm_list_topic_types to see valid values.

languageModelTools.name: wm_delete_topic
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Soft-delete a topic and cascade soft-delete to its workstream_topics and entry_topics link rows in a single transaction. The topic falls out of the tree and out of every linked workstream's Topics section, but a future re-link (via wm_link_workstream_topic or wm_link_entry_topic) will undelete it transparently. Returns counts of affected rows per table.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Soft-delete a topic (cascades to its link rows)

slug.description: Slug of the topic to soft-delete.

languageModelTools.name: wm_restore_topic
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Restore a soft-deleted topic by clearing its deleted_at. Restores only the topic row itself — link rows in workstream_topics and entry_topics remain soft-deleted and can be re-activated individually via wm_link_workstream_topic or wm_link_entry_topic. Returns count of restored rows. No-op (returns zeros) if the topic is not currently soft-deleted.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Restore a soft-deleted topic

slug.description: Slug of the topic to restore.

languageModelTools.name: wm_link_workstream_topic
languageModelTools.modelDescription:
Pin a topic (and optionally its graph neighbourhood) to a workstream. Idempotent. When `traversal` is omitted or 'self' (default), behaves exactly as before: attaches only the seed topic. Pass a traversal mode to attach a wider set in one call:
• 'self' — seed topic only (default).
• 'childrenOf' — seed + direct children.
• 'immediateFamilyOf' — seed + direct parents + direct children + siblings (children of those parents).
• 'recursiveFamilyOf' — seed + full connected subgraph (all ancestors, descendants, siblings transitively).
Closed topics are skipped during traversal unless `includeClosed` is true. Cycle-safe: a visited-set ensures termination even on diamond-shaped DAGs. If the topic slug doesn't exist yet, a stub topic is auto-created (topic_created: true). Soft-deleted link rows are restored (link_restored: true). `focused` applies only to the seed topic, never to traversed neighbours. Returns `linked` (array of newly created/restored links), `skipped_already_linked` (slugs that were already active), and the resolved `traversal` mode.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Link a topic (and optional neighbourhood) to a workstream

topic_slug.description: Slug of the seed topic (auto-created if missing).

focused.description: Optional. true = mark the seed topic as focused in the workstream; false = clear focus (link itself stays); omitted = preserve existing focus state. Never applied to traversed neighbours.

traversal.description: Graph-traversal mode. Defaults to 'self' (seed topic only). 'childrenOf' adds direct children. 'immediateFamilyOf' adds parents, children, and siblings. 'recursiveFamilyOf' adds the full connected subgraph.

includeClosed.description: When true, closed topics encountered during traversal are included. Defaults to false. Has no effect when traversal is 'self'.

languageModelTools.name: wm_unlink_workstream_topic
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Soft-delete the workstream_topics link row between a workstream and a topic. The topic itself is untouched (it may still be linked to other workstreams via entries). Returns the count of removed link rows (0 if none was active).
languageModelTools.userDescription: Unlink a topic from a workstream

languageModelTools.name: wm_link_entry_topic
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Tag a journal entry with a topic (M:N). Idempotent. Auto-creates a stub topic (title = humanized slug, status 'open', empty body) if topic_slug is unknown — flagged in the response as topic_created. ALSO auto-creates a workstream_topics row linking the topic to the entry's workstream if one doesn't exist; if such a row exists but is soft-deleted, it is restored. This is the bit of magic that makes the tree useful: any entry tagged with a topic causes that topic to appear under its workstream's Topics group without a separate wm_link_workstream_topic call. If the entry, its session, or its workstream is soft-deleted, the link is rejected. If the topic itself is soft-deleted, it is undeleted (so re-linking a 'restored' topic is implicit).
languageModelTools.userDescription: Tag an entry with a topic (auto-links workstream too)

topic_slug.description: Slug of the topic (auto-created if missing).

languageModelTools.name: wm_unlink_entry_topic
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Soft-delete the entry_topics link row between an entry and a topic. Does NOT touch the workstream_topics link — other entries in the same workstream may still link the topic. Use wm_unlink_workstream_topic if you also want to remove the workstream pin. Returns the count of removed link rows (0 if none was active).
languageModelTools.userDescription: Untag an entry from a topic

languageModelTools.name: wm_link_topic_parent
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Link a topic to a parent topic (DAG, M:N). A topic may have 0 or more parents and appears under each of them in the Topics tree. Idempotent: if an active link already exists, the existing row is returned unchanged; if a soft-deleted link exists for the same pair, it is restored (link_restored: true). Rejects self-links and cycles — a link is refused when child_slug is already in the ancestor closure walked upward from parent_slug. Both topics must exist and not be soft-deleted; topics are NOT auto-created (use wm_create_topic first if needed). Closing a parent has NO cascade effect on children.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Link a topic to a parent topic (DAG)

child_slug.description: Slug of the child topic (the one nested under the parent).

languageModelTools.name: wm_unlink_topic_parent
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Soft-delete a topic parent link. Idempotent; returns the count of removed rows (0 if no active link existed for the pair). Other parent/child relationships of the two topics are untouched.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Unlink a topic from a parent topic

languageModelTools.name: wm_list_topic_types
languageModelTools.modelDescription: List the rows in the `topic_types` registry table. Each row returns id (the value stored in `topics.topic_type`), label (human-readable singular display name), icon (VS Code codicon id, see https://microsoft.github.io/vscode-codicons/), description (one-sentence semantics), body_template (markdown scaffold with H2 section headers; empty string means no template), created_at, and updated_at. Call this before passing `topic_type` to wm_create_topic / wm_update_topic / wm_list_topics to know which ids are valid — the topic-mutating tools reject unknown ids server-side with a clear error.
languageModelTools.userDescription: List available topic types

languageModelTools.name: wm_create_topic_type
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Create a topic-type row in `topic_types`. Requires id, label, icon, description. Rejects duplicate ids. Returns the created row.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Create a topic type

languageModelTools.name: wm_get_topic_type
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Fetch a topic-type row by id and include the count of topics that currently reference it.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Get one topic type by id

languageModelTools.name: wm_update_topic_type
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Partially update a topic-type row by id. Supports label, icon, description, and body_template fields. body_template is a markdown blob with H2 section headers — when non-empty, wm_create_topic reshapes the caller's body into this structure via LLM. Pass an empty string to clear it. Bumps `updated_at`. Returns the updated row.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Update a topic type

label.description: Display label (must not be empty if provided).

body_template.description: Markdown body template with H2 section headers. When non-empty, wm_create_topic reshapes the body via LLM to fit these sections. Pass an empty string to clear the template.

languageModelTools.name: wm_delete_topic_type
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Delete a topic-type row by id. Seeded ids (`topic`, `feature`, `task`) are protected and cannot be deleted. Deletion is refused when any topics still reference the type; error includes blocker count.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Delete a topic type

languageModelTools.name: wm_get_panel_data
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns the exact data the Working Memory panel UI is rendering — workstreams, sessions, topics, and topic types as the webview sees them. Use to verify what's visible in the panel, or to debug discrepancies between DB state and UI. Input is an optional `tab`: 'active' | 'archive' | 'topics' | 'topic-types' returns a single `PanelData` for that tab; 'all' (default, also used when input is omitted) returns `{ active, archive, topics, topicTypes }` — the full shape from getAllPanelData(). Output items use tagged-union shapes from src/panelData.ts and are fully JSON-serializable. Pure read, no side effects.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Get the data currently rendered by the Working Memory panel

tab.description: Which panel tab to return. Defaults to 'all', which returns the full {active, archive, topics, topicTypes} shape.

languageModelTools.name: wm_create_alert
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Raise a durable, structured 'needs attention' alert against one or more topics. `description` is required; `title` (optional, friendly short label) defaults to the first ~60 chars of description; `recommended_action` optional. `topic_slugs` are the M:N targets and are REQUIRED — at least one must be supplied. Each MUST already exist (an unknown or soft-deleted slug is rejected — no stub creation). The alert is created with status 'alert'. Dedupe: `dedupe_key` is always populated — caller-supplied if given, otherwise derived from hash(created_by + description + sorted topic_slugs). If an OPEN alert (status != 'closed') already holds that key, it is upserted (description/recommended_action refreshed, re-raised to 'alert') instead of inserting a duplicate; the response's `deduped` flag says which happened. Returns the alert row, its linked topics, and `deduped`.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Raise an alert against one or more topics

title.description: Short, friendly title. Optional; defaults to the first ~60 chars of description.

recommended_action.description: Suggested next step. Optional; defaults to empty.

topic_slugs.description: Slugs of the topics this alert flags. Required — at least one. Each must already exist and not be soft-deleted.

dedupe_key.description: Optional caller-supplied dedupe identity. Derived from created_by + description + sorted topic_slugs when omitted.

languageModelTools.name: wm_get_alert
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Fetch a single alert by numeric id, including its linked topic slugs. Mirrors wm_get_topic / wm_get_workstream. Errors if the alert does not exist.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Get an alert and its linked topics

languageModelTools.name: wm_list_alerts
languageModelTools.modelDescription: List alerts, ordered by severity (alert, then informational, then closed) and recency. By default returns the active queue (alert + informational); pass status to filter. Optionally scope to one topic with topic_slug. Each alert includes its linked topic slugs.
languageModelTools.userDescription: List alerts (active queue by default)

status.description: Filter by status. Defaults to 'active' (alert + informational). 'all' includes closed.

topic_slug.description: Only return alerts linked to this topic.

languageModelTools.name: wm_update_alert
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Partial-update a single alert (mirrors wm_update_workstream / wm_update_topic). Edit `title`, `description` and/or `recommended_action`, and drive the status lifecycle via the `status` arg: 'alert' (active, rings bells) -> 'informational' (downgraded, quiet, stays in the active queue) -> 'closed' (terminal, leaves the queue and frees its dedupe_key). Any change bumps updated_at. Returns the updated alert with its topics.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Update an alert or change its status

description.description: New description. Cannot be empty if provided.

status.description: New status. 'alert' = active, 'informational' = downgraded but still in queue, 'closed' = terminal.

languageModelTools.name: wm_link_alert_topic
languageModelTools.displayName: Working Memory: Link Alert to Topic
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Link an existing alert to an existing topic (M:N). Idempotent. The topic must already exist and not be soft-deleted — no stub creation (unlike wm_link_entry_topic).
languageModelTools.userDescription: Link an alert to a topic

topic_slug.description: Slug of the topic to link. Must already exist.

languageModelTools.name: wm_unlink_alert_topic
languageModelTools.displayName: Working Memory: Unlink Alert from Topic
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Remove the link between an alert and a topic. Idempotent — `unlinked` is false when there was nothing to remove.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Unlink an alert from a topic

topic_slug.description: Slug of the topic to unlink.
